summary: High initial-token latency on chat completions after runtime 1.5 + smart-router rollout
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports noticeably slower chat responses where there is a visible pause before the assistant emits the first token. This started shortly after our runtime 1.5 rollout combined with a new smart-router policy that prefers model variants with 'cost-optim' labels in low-cost cells.

Impact:
- Several production chat flows at Acme Fintech have median initial-token latency increase from ~220ms to ~1.1s and p95 ~2.4s.
- Affects user-facing chat widgets for ~18% of requests that route through the new policy.
- Higher perceived lag causing customer support escalations and potential user churn risk.

Environment:
- Redwood prod, us-east-1 region, Dedicated pool for Acme Fintech.
- Runtime version: 1.5.0 (rolled 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC).
- Smart-router policy: prefer-cost-variants v2 (rolled 2026-03-09 01:50 UTC).

Steps to reproduce:
1) Make a ChatCompletion request with streaming enabled using model redwood/gptj-6b-qat-v2 pinned for customer account on the dedicated pool.
2) Observe full connection establishment; monitor time between request acceptance and first streamed token.
3) Repeat ~50 times to sample distribution.

Expected behavior:
- First token emission should be ~200-300ms median for this model and dedicated pool.

Actual behavior:
- Median initial-token latency observed ~1.1s, p95 ~2.4s for affected requests. Not consistent across all requests — correlates to requests routed to specific low-cost variant shards.

Logs / traces (excerpt):
- access-log: request_id=6f9b3a start=2026-03-09T02:12:07.123Z accept=2026-03-09T02:12:07.130Z first_token=2026-03-09T02:12:08.302Z
- serving-trace: kernel_warmup=480ms, load_model_variant=180ms, kv_cache_lookup=40ms, queue_wait=200ms, grpc_handshake=30ms
- router-log: chosen_variant=cheap-variant-34 reason=policy:prefer-cost-variants v2

Attachments: performance traces and flamegraphs uploaded to customer-support S3 (s3://redwood-support/sup-13724/).
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Use customer account credentials on dedicated pool in us-east-1. 2) Send stream-enabled chat completion to model redwood/gptj-6b-qat-v2. 3) Capture timestamps for request accepted and first token emitted. 4) Repeat to collect a latency distribution.
investigation_notes: 03/09 04:20 - Initial triage: Support confirmed impact and escalated to SRE. Captured traces and customer repro steps.
03/09 06:05 - SRE observed correlation between higher initial-token latency and requests routed to 'cheap-variant-*' shards that use a different kernel selection and aggressive quantization profile.

03/09 08:10 - Eng hypothesis: slow 'kernel warmup' path triggered when runtime routes to variants that haven't been hot for the current sequence-length distribution. Warmup cost ~400-600ms per request leading to median shift.
03/09 09:30 - Additional hypothesis: smart-router's new 'prefer-cost-variants' policy increases traffic to underutilized nodes, causing higher cold-start rates and queue_wait spikes (~150-300ms).
03/09 10:45 - Experiment: force-route 200 sample requests to 'low-latency' variant; median initial-token latency returned to ~230ms. Confirms routing + variant-warmup as root factors.

03/09 11:20 - Identified related change in PR router#187 that adjusted scoring weights; linked PRs for follow-up. Also flagged PR serving-runtime#4213 that changed kernel selection ordering for qat quantized models.
03/09 12:00 - Customer requested mitigation; recommended immediate temporary pin to previous model variant + rollback of router policy for their account while a fix is prepared.
comments: Priya Shah (Support) - 2026-03-09T05:30Z: Received escalation from Acme Fintech. They reported significant pause before assistant starts typing. Collecting traces and sample requests now.

Miguel Alvarez (SRE) - 2026-03-09T06:50Z: I see patterns where 'cheap-variant' nodes show kernel_warmup ~0.45s more than baseline. Traces attached. Looks like kernel selection picks a slower execution path for some quant profiles.

Samira Khan (Backend Eng) - 2026-03-09T08:30Z: Confirmed that runtime 1.5 changed preferred kernel for qat models when sequence_length < 128. This falls back to a different micro-kernel that has a higher one-time setup cost.

Ethan Cole (Platform Eng) - 2026-03-09T09:50Z: Applied an account-scoped routing override for Acme Fintech to prefer low-latency variants. Observed immediate improvement in customer metrics. Preparing a short-term config patch to router to reduce selection of cold variants.
Priya Shah (Support) - 2026-03-09T10:05Z: Customer confirmed improvement after override; still monitoring. Marking customer as 'Waiting' for patch deployment.

Samira Khan (Backend Eng) - 2026-03-11T14:40Z: Deployed hotfix that changes kernel selection ordering to avoid the high-warmup micro-kernel for short sequences and added a warmup cache for infrequently-used variants. Router policy weights adjusted to include a latency penalty term.
Ethan Cole (Platform Eng) - 2026-03-11T16:00Z: Rolling metrics show median returns to ~250ms, p95 ~600ms for the affected customer. Closing the incident after customer validation.
Acme Fintech (Customer) - 2026-03-12T09:22Z: We've validated on our side — initial response times are back to acceptable levels. Thanks for the quick action.
resolution_notes: Workaround: pinned Acme account to previous low-latency variant and applied a per-account routing override within 2 hours of detection. Fix: hotfix in serving-runtime to prefer the warm micro-kernel only for long sequences and added a light-weight warmup cache for cold variants; router policy updated to include latency penalty in scoring. Deployed 2026-03-11. Monitoring: added dashboard for 'initial-token latency by variant' and an alert if median > 500ms for >5 minutes for dedicated pools. Follow-up: schedule a smaller-scale canary of runtime 1.5 kernel ordering changes and harden autoscaling warmup for underutilized shards.
